mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in WORKPLACES is a lead indicator of broader daytime movement suppression, and it will pull RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks as commuting-linked errands and discretionary shopping remain depressed.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from 3.3 at t-1w to -16.9 at t-0w while TRANSIT fell from -3.6 to -21.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not remain below its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days despite continued weakness in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL rises above 5 points, households substitute away from out-of-home consumption and retail visits are reduced immediately, keeping RETAIL_REC lower within one week and for the following month.
failure_condition: A week after RESIDENTIAL exceeds 5, RETAIL_REC fails to decline relative to the prior week or rebounds above its recent average.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent collapse in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES amplifies retail weakness because fewer commuters and fewer workplace trips jointly reduce incidental shopping, producing lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both dropped sharply at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay depressed for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not fall below its prior 4-week mean, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid broad-based downturn across TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, and GROCERY_PHARM signals tightening movement constraints, which will continue to suppress discretionary retail demand and keep RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -15 points or WORKPLACES falls below -10 points
failure_condition: If either mobility restriction proxy breaches the threshold but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week average within 28 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Weakening PARKS activity alongside falling RETAIL_REC reflects a general pullback in nonessential outings; if PARKS remains negative, retail visits will stay below the recent four-week average over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from 8.0 at t-3w to -11.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS stays negative for two weeks but RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 28-day mean, the demand-substitution story is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous rise in RESIDENTIAL and fall in TRANSIT indicates weather- or season-driven staying home, and that pattern should keep RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks relative to the prior four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose to 5.9 while TRANSIT fell to -21.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while TRANSIT stays deeply negative but RETAIL_REC improves over the next 28 days, the seasonal-stay-home mechanism is false.

mechanism_narrative: Once GROCERY_PHARM drops below -10, households are likely responding to severe containment or supply frictions, and that shock will spill into lower retail visitation within two weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains below -10 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not fall below its last-4-week mean, the spillover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized decline in PARKS and TRANSIT signals a citywide reduction in out-of-home activity, and that combined contraction will push RETAIL_REC lower over the next month by reducing both leisure and commuting spillovers.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 8.0 to -11.1 while TRANSIT fell from 0.9 to -21.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS and TRANSIT remain weak for four weeks but RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises versus the previous 28 days, the joint-demand decline hypothesis fails.
